description: The agent must: (1) Initialize the memory-attention-router DB using `memory_router.py init`. (2) Add the old 'verbose JSON blobs' preference memory. (3) Add the NEW 'under 3 bullets' preference memory using `replaces_memory_id` pointing to the old one — this must trigger the old memory becoming inactive (is_active=0) with `replaced_by_memory_id` set and `retired_reason` stored. (4) Add the deployment procedure memory (pre-flight → manifest → verify → summary) and the shortcut procedure memory. (5) Add the OOM episode memory. (6) Use the `reflect` command with `create_procedure=true` for the Q3 sprint outcome, which generates both a reflection memory (→ pitfalls_to_avoid) and a procedure memory. (7) Use the `refresh` command to deactivate the stale 'ad-hoc kubectl' summary, marking it inactive with a refresh_reason. (8) Optionally add a `supports` edge from the reflection to the pre-flight procedure (to help it outrank the shortcut procedure despite lower raw importance). (9) Route an `executor` packet — the agent must know that executor reads `preference` type memories (a 'Key update' in the docs), so `hard_constraints` must contain the bullets constraint even in execution; `procedures_to_follow` should have the pre-flight procedure; `pitfalls_to_avoid` should include the OOM/skip-preflight lesson. All packet fields must respect caps (hard_constraints ≤ 4, procedures ≤ 3, pitfalls ≤ 3, selected_memory_ids ≤ 5, relevant_facts ≤ 3). (10) Route a `critic` packet — critic reads reflection, preference, summary types. (11) Write `memory_audit_report.json` with both packet outputs, memory IDs, retirement summary. Key proprietary traps: `replaces_memory_id` triggers automatic retirement; executor role reads `preference` type (not just procedure/episode); `reflects` creates both reflection AND procedure memory when `create_procedure=true`; packet field type mapping (preference→hard_constraints, procedure→procedures_to_follow, reflection→pitfalls_to_avoid); all compactness caps.
